newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia gets 89.8 pct of '96 revenues after 11 mos.
newsitem.headline: Estonia gets 89.8 pct of '96 revenues after 11 mos.

text.p: Estonia collected 11.845 billion kroons, or 89.8 percent, of planned 1996 revenues by the end of November, the finance ministry said on Wednesday.
Collection was below 1995, when 91.2 percent of revenues were collected after 11 months, the ministry said in a statement.
It said personal income tax brought in 3.89 billion kroons and company tax contributed 840 million kroons. Those were 92.7 percent and 93 percent of the planned year totals.
Sales tax brought in 4.7 billion kroons, or 89.6 percent of planned sales revenue, and excise duty 1.53 billion kroons, or 80.8 percent of planned revenues from that source.
Estonia has a balanced state budget by law but the International Monetary Fund has recently expressed worries over the whole public sector deficit, which includes borrowings by local governments.
